Name: Backend for Frontend (BFF)
Pattern: Backend tailored to a user experience with boundaries informed by client needs and team ownership
Use Case: Mobile and web experiences with different payloads or orchestration needs
Strengths: Tailored responses can reduce over-fetching and round trips; independent client-oriented deployment
Weaknesses: Additional service operations; duplicated orchestration; downstream failures affect aggregate responses
Gotcha: Similar iOS and Android experiences may share a BFF; keep shared domain invariants in domain services while allowing experience-specific orchestration; define deadlines and partial-response behavior

Name: Offline-First Sync
Pattern: Read from a local source of truth and persist pending writes for later synchronization
Use Case: Mobile apps that need critical reads or selected writes without reliable connectivity
Strengths: Responsive cached reads; durable pending changes when explicitly implemented
Weaknesses: Local data may be stale or incomplete; conflict handling and queue persistence require design
Gotcha: Choose conflict policy per operation; Firestore uses last-write-wins for the same document; version checks or explicit merges may suit other backends; test concurrent edits and process death as well as airplane mode

Name: Push Notification Delivery
Pattern: Best-effort server-to-device alerts or invalidation hints via APNs and FCM
Use Case: Notify users or prompt reconciliation with authoritative server state
Strengths: Platform-managed delivery avoids frequent polling; native notification integration
Weaknesses: Delivery may be delayed or dropped; notification permission and app state affect behavior; registration lifecycle management
Gotcha: Upload current registrations with timestamps; stop sends on APNs 410 or FCM UNREGISTERED until valid registration; treat FCM INVALID_ARGUMENT as invalid registration only with a valid payload; reconcile on foreground because provider acceptance is not delivery

Name: GraphQL for Mobile
Pattern: Typed client-selected fields with server-enforced demand controls
Use Case: Mobile screens requiring different data shapes over constrained networks
Strengths: Can reduce response over-fetching and client round trips; typed API contracts
Weaknesses: Resolver N+1 and expensive queries remain possible; cache and authorization design are still required
Gotcha: Bound list sizes and operation depth plus breadth and batch size; enforce cost budgets and timeouts; consider trusted-document allowlists for first-party apps; field selection does not bound backend work

Name: CDN for API Responses
Pattern: Cache explicitly shareable API representations at the edge with bounded freshness
Use Case: Public catalogs and non-sensitive configuration shared across mobile clients
Strengths: Cache hits can reduce latency and origin load; validators reduce unchanged transfers
Weaknesses: Stale data and incorrect cache keys can expose personalized data; application caches need their own policy
Gotcha: Use private to exclude shared caches and no-store for sensitive responses that must not be stored; no-cache requires validation rather than prohibiting storage; set max-age and s-maxage deliberately and include representation variants in cache keys; do not publicly cache personalized feature flags

Name: API Versioning for Mobile
Pattern: Maintain compatible contracts within a version and introduce new versions for breaking changes
Use Case: Installed mobile clients that update on different schedules
Strengths: Decouples backend rollout from app updates; explicit deprecation and compatibility contracts
Weaknesses: Parallel versions add maintenance cost; old clients and database migrations constrain retirement
Gotcha: Do not remove fields or change types and defaults within a supported version; test older clients against new servers; set retirement policy using client-version telemetry; app review and installation are separate rollout steps with no assumed fixed review duration

Name: Optimistic UI Updates
Pattern: Render a provisional local result then reconcile it with the authoritative mutation response
Use Case: Reversible interactions such as likes and edits where failure can be explained
Strengths: Immediate local feedback can mask network latency without claiming server completion
Weaknesses: Rejection and overlapping mutations complicate rollback; an optimistic cache is not a durable offline queue
Gotcha: Track pending and failed operations; replace temporary IDs with server IDs; reconcile or roll back only the affected optimistic state; a timeout leaves the server outcome uncertain so retries need idempotency or status reconciliation

Name: Token Refresh Flow
Pattern: Refresh access tokens when needed while execution and connectivity are available
Use Case: Maintain mobile sessions subject to authorization-server expiration and revocation policy
Strengths: Short-lived access tokens; fewer interactive sign-ins while refresh credentials remain valid
Weaknesses: Refresh credentials require protected storage; concurrent rotation can invalidate sessions; background execution is not assured
Gotcha: Public-client refresh tokens must rotate or be sender-constrained; serialize refresh per session and persist replacement credentials before releasing waiters; stop on invalid_grant and require reauthentication rather than loop

Name: Image Optimization Pipeline
Pattern: Resize and encode bounded image variants and cache them by representation
Use Case: Mobile image delivery matched to display dimensions and actual decoder capabilities
Strengths: Can reduce transferred bytes and decode work; savings depend on content and quality settings
Weaknesses: Encoding cost and variant proliferation; format support depends on client decoder and version
Gotcha: Negotiate formats using accurate Accept capabilities or explicit variants with a compatible fallback; do not infer WebP or AVIF support from OS name alone; key caches by size and format and honor Vary when negotiating; measure bytes and decode time

Name: App Startup Optimization
Pattern: Render minimal useful content without blocking on network and defer non-critical initialization
Use Case: Improve first-frame and usable-content latency on cold and warm launches
Strengths: Cached bootstrap data can improve perceived responsiveness during slow connectivity
Weaknesses: Stale or missing cache and main-thread work can still delay usable content; prefetching consumes data and battery
Gotcha: Measure Android TTID and TTFD separately on representative devices; use account-scoped last-known-good bootstrap data only when acceptable and refresh asynchronously; handle empty caches explicitly; set measured budgets rather than promise a universal sub-second launch

Name: Background Work Scheduling
Pattern: Schedule resumable sync using Android WorkManager or appropriate Apple background APIs
Use Case: Deferred synchronization that must tolerate suspension and changing network or battery conditions
Strengths: OS-coordinated work can conserve power; persisted checkpoints support resumption
Weaknesses: Start times are system-controlled; work can be stopped or deferred; push does not guarantee execution
Gotcha: WorkManager periodic minimum is 15 minutes not an exact cadence; Apple background pushes use content-available=1 with apns-push-type=background and priority 5 and allow up to 30 seconds when delivered; reserve Android FCM high priority for time-sensitive user-visible content; checkpoint and reconcile on foreground

Name: Native OAuth Authorization Code with PKCE
Pattern: Use authorization code with PKCE S256 through an external user-agent
Use Case: Native mobile sign-in without embedding reusable client secrets or collecting provider passwords
Strengths: PKCE protects intercepted authorization codes; browser security boundary supports shared sign-in state
Weaknesses: Redirect ownership and provider configuration need care; PKCE does not replace API authorization
Gotcha: Register native apps as public clients; use a system browser or secure browser tab rather than an embedded WebView; validate transaction state and exact registered redirects with the loopback-port exception; prefer app-claimed HTTPS redirects where supported; never treat a bundled shared secret as confidential

Name: Mobile Request Retries and Idempotency
Pattern: Persist operation identity and retry only transient failures with a server-enforced deduplication contract
Use Case: Queued mobile writes and interrupted requests whose server outcome is unknown
Strengths: Safe replays can avoid duplicate business effects; bounded backoff reduces synchronized load
Weaknesses: Requires durable server records and concurrency handling; expired deduplication records can allow duplicate execution
Gotcha: Reuse one key and unchanged payload per logical operation; scope deduplication to authenticated caller and operation and make it atomic with the effect; bound retries with exponential backoff and jitter and honor Retry-After; stop permanent failures; reconcile uncertain outcomes after key expiry rather than blindly replay
